new.n: Lothrop: B&NM end of steel and Minnesota Logging Co. headquarters (1895)
new.pl: NW corner of sec. 31 T141N R30W on the old B&NM line between Hackensack and Walker, Cass County
new.st: King (1981): by early 1895 Lothrop, 51 miles from Brainerd, was the end of steel of the Brainerd & Northern Minnesota and the woods headquarters of the Minnesota Logging Co., with two hotels, a warehouse, a boarding house for 100, an office, a three-stall enginehouse and shops, on "one of the prettiest lakes". "Today, Lothrop has vanished completely." The 1901 Jewett sectional map of Cass and Crow Wing counties shows Lothrop station on the B&NM at the NW corner of sec. 31, with a spur running east through secs. 30, 29 and 28 and a lake just west; Hunters station was about 2.5 miles north.
new.t: Look on the 1938 aerial and LiDAR for the enginehouse pit, hotel cellars and the spur grade east of the old line. Private land: ask first.
src: Frank A. King, Minnesota Logging Railroads (1981), pp 52-53
Jewett & Son, Sectional map of Cass and Crow Wing Counties, Minnesota (1901)
pinev: 1901 sectional map puts the station at the NW corner of sec. 31 (T/R read from the margin as T141N R30W, which matches King's 51 miles from Brainerd); placed from the BLM PLSS corner (about 200 m).

1894 Foote plat book: village inset puts the flour mill at the east end of Main St on the North Branch Zumbro, and the Zumbrota township plate places that in the SE quarter of the SE quarter of sec. 29 T110N R15W; placed from the BLM PLSS section (about 200 m).

vs-2064877.st: The 1894 Foote plat book has a Forest Mills village inset: the town lay on the south bank of a big bend of the North Branch of the Zumbro, with the Milwaukee Road along the north edge and the station and post office on the track. The flour mill (two big buildings) stood at the east end, on the river at the foot of Main St, with a race across the river and a cooper shop nearby. There were a butter-tub factory, a creamery and School No. 101 in the village blocks. The pin now sits at the mill site, in the SE quarter of the SE quarter of sec. 29.
src: Foote, Plat book of Goodhue County, Minnesota (1894), plate 5 inset and Zumbrota twp p. 41

pinev: 1896 Wabasha atlas: Henry Feddern's 123.50 acres in the SE quarter of sec. 2 T110N R10W on the river shore, house dot near the east line; the 1893 Herald says Feddern's house was Roe's surviving Teepeota house. Placed at that dot from the BLM PLSS section (about 300 m).

cd-teepeota-townsite-1856.st: The 1896 Wabasha County atlas shows Henry Feddern's 123.50 acres in the SE quarter of sec. 2 T110N R10W on the river shore, with a house dot near the east line, and "Evans & Tenney" land in the north part of sec. 3. Since Feddern's house was Roe's surviving Teepeota house, the pin now sits there.
src: Standard Atlas of Wabasha County, Minnesota (1896), Greenfield twp p. 15
